Mechanical exfoliation can produce ultrathin flakes, but the resulting flakes are often irregular in shape, randomly distributed, variable in thickness and remains a low-throughput approach12,13.

Liquid-phase synthesis offers a more direct route by forming monolayer and few-layer flakes directly on substrates under controlled crystallization conditions but existing methods commonly suffer from uncontrolled nucleation, aggregation, limited lateral size, and low yields of monolayer and few-layer crystals14.
